pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/companion/approvals/approval_exec_browser.rs:484 browser_login hand-writes a whitelist-miss error with no next command, bypassing the closed RefusalCode::OriginNotAllowed hint ('call browser_request_site ...'). approval_lifecycle.rs:192 then folds that text into Athena's persisted episode, so her next turn has nothing to act on.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/companion/approvals/approval_exec_browser.rs:484 Rewritten at the call site instead of the one door, and it names no next command. Its neighbours at 486-501 do carry one, which is the call-site decay the technique warns about. refusal_to_app_error (line 217) does preserve code and hint for refusals that come through the gate.

src-tauri/src/commands/companion/approvals/approval_exec_browser.rs:538 Login replays refs the scan copied verbatim from an earlier snapshot and persisted in the DB (scan_prompt.rs:83). hands.js scopes every ref to one document and a random per-document map, so these refs cannot resolve on a later page load. The failure is loud (unknown_ref), not a wrong click, but the login is valid only by coincidence. The rule is to persist a role+name locator or snapshot at execution time.

src-tauri/src/commands/companion/approvals/approval_exec_browser.rs:187 The gate decides from the registry's Action::effect(). BROWSER_WRITE_TOOLS (line 70) is a hand-drawn restricted-caller allowlist, but a test checks each member classifies as Effect::Write. The file admits write_action mirrors mcp::action_for, a second table it plans to retire.
